inputs.name: item count
inputs.note: exactly "1 item" is the flat price; any other answer, and no answer, is hourly billing with the minimum billable hour

inputs.name: area
inputs.note: the code takes parseInt() of the chosen LABEL (2, 10, 25, 50) and falls back to 2. The numbers are written down here as data so that no label text is parsed. KNOWN LIMIT, stated not fixed: the top answer is "50 sq ft or more" and the engine prices it as exactly 50, so a larger area is under-estimated; an exact-count capture for the open-ended band is the same decision as the dormant item_count_overflow_formula (v9.6).

inputs.name: patch
inputs.note: applied to every drywall repair, whatever the answers

inputs.name: install type
inputs.note: the code matches the chosen label against /new hole/i or /drilling/i; every other answer, and no answer, is the swap rate. Recovered here as an explicit option-to-branch table so that the meaning no longer depends on label wording.

inputs.name: units
inputs.note: units = the booked quantity. The code first tries an `answers.unit_count` key; no intake module of that name exists (see dropped_legacy_consumed_keys).

inputs.name: exact count
inputs.note: applies to the options that name this formula (formula_id) and carry a qty_value: the open-ended top band prices its own flat modifier plus the overflow rate beyond the service anchor

inputs.name: cabinet frames
inputs.note: each count is the chosen option's qty_value; the code falls back to parseInt() of the label, which would read "6 or more" as 6 and is not reproduced

inputs.name: tile count
inputs.note: tile count = the booked quantity; `answers.tile_count` is not an intake module.
